description: Magick Agency at a glance: the agency dialer (live attempts, throughput, compliance, pacing), voice capacity, identity and mail, analysis, and runtime health — one pane per agency deployment, filtered by environment and service. Every query selects agency's service names only.
title: Magick Agency — Overview

panels.description:
Agency capacity in use, split by what it is doing: the dialer's campaign attempts by state, and the soft phone's live calls stacked on top. `dialing` is capacity committed to phones that may never answer; `bridged` is conversations actually earning. The split is the point: a flat concurrency number cannot tell 40 phones ringing from 40 conversations, which is the blind spot that made the 2026-09-08 pilot's bridge rate unreadable. Soft-phone calls hold carrier slots exactly like attempts and pacing's headroom subtracts them, but they belong to no campaign, so without the second series this panel showed headroom pacing did not have.

REDUCED WITH `max` ACROSS REPLICAS, THEN SUMMED: the underlying SQL is fleet-wide and every replica publishes the identical series, so `max by` each series' own labels collapses the replicas (a bare `sum` would report one multiple of the truth per replica), and only then are campaigns and tenants summed. Same rule as the abandonment gauge beside it.

`ringing` is a legal attempt state that nothing in the campaign dialer writes — expect no attempt series for it (the soft phone does write it). An empty panel (rather than a zero) means the 90s staleness TTL expired and no replica is publishing: treat that as the metric being down, not the dialer idle.
panels.title: Agency Dialer — Live Calls by State (campaign + soft phone)

targets.expr: sum by (state) (max by (tenant_id, campaign_id, state) (agency_live_attempts_current{deployment_environment=~"$environment", service_name=~"$service_name", tenant_id=~"$tenant_id"}))

panels.title: Agency Dialer — Abandonment
panels.description: Rolling 24h abandonment rate per campaign, in percent — the compliance number. The 3% line is the usual regulatory ceiling; adjust to your jurisdiction.

panels.title: Agency Dialer — Throughput
panels.description: Answered vs abandoned, plus why the pacing engine dialed nothing on a tick. (No billing series: agency has no billing.)

Every pre-dial gate decision by `gate` and `action`. `cleared`/`dial` is throughput; `suppress` arms are per-contact (DNC, invalid phone, calling window); `gate="dnc_unavailable"` with `action="halt"` is the campaign-wide compliance halt — the DNC registry (a Postgres read of `dnc_entries`) could not answer. `agy-dnc-unavailable` pages on it. Carries `campaign_id`, not `tenant_id`, so the Tenant filter does not apply.
panels.title: Pre-dial Gate Outcomes

panels.description: Dial attempts per second as they settle, by outcome (`agency_attempt_hold_seconds_count`: one observation per attempt). The agency dialer's call volume; agency has no billed-attempt counter.
panels.title: Settled Attempts by Outcome

panels.description:
THE PACING PANEL. Agent-minutes consumed per minute of wall clock, split by the outcome that consumed them — i.e. how many agents' worth of time each kind of attempt is eating right now.

Read it as a budget. `connected` is the work; everything else is waiting. The 2026-09-08 pilot ran 26% talk / 60% waiting / 13% wrap-up, and the single largest waiting block was busy signals at ~37s each — which no ring timeout can shorten, because a busy phone never rings. That distinction is only visible because this is split by outcome; an aggregate 'average wait' pointed every previous analysis at the wrong lever.

What each bucket implies: `busy`/`failed` high = carrier signalling latency (not tunable here); `no_answer` high = a ring timeout would pay, which needs a cancel-capable carrier; `canceled` high = our own teardown latency; `connected` high = talk time, and NOT waste.

Per-replica histogram — aggregate with `sum(rate(...))`, never `max`. The opposite of the SQL-derived gauges on this dashboard.
panels.title: Agency Dialer — Where Seat Time Goes

panels.description:
How long ONE attempt holds an agent, from the dial to the attempt ending, by outcome. The per-attempt view of the panel beside it.

This series settles a disagreement that blocked the pacing decision twice: the code comment on `CARRIER_END_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` says VoiceLink reports terminal state at dial+45-75s, while the pilot's own decomposition measured a flat ~31s. Nothing measured it, so both numbers survived. Read `no_answer`/`busy` here and the argument is over.

Wrap-up is deliberately EXCLUDED and has its own panel: folding it in would make the one bucket an operator must not try to shrink look like the biggest opportunity on the chart.
panels.title: Agency Dialer — Attempt Hold Time by Outcome

panels.description:
Dial → carrier answer, for attempts that answered. Two decisions read this one distribution:

1. THE RING TIMEOUT WORTH SETTING — where the curve flattens, and what the tail beyond it would forgo. There is no ring timeout on the agency dial path today: `ringTimeoutSeconds` is populated only from a DID on the inbound path, `agency_campaigns` has no such column, and on VoiceLink the dial request accepts no such parameter at all.

2. THE OVER-DIAL ARITHMETIC — §11's marginal-abandonment formula takes a flat answer rate `p`, but the real exposure of a surplus dial is how tightly two answers can CLUSTER, which is this distribution's shape. p50 near p99 means clustering is likely and over-dialing is worse than the formula says.

Under D1 a voicemail pickup is an answer like any other, so this is the carrier's view — the same view the abandonment predicate takes.
panels.title: Agency Dialer — Answer Latency

panels.description:
THE LATE-BINDING ROLLOUT GATE, finally measurable. §7.3 gates the week-long hold on 'bind-latency p99 <150ms and zero bind failures', and §11 carried that criterion as NOT INSTRUMENTED from the day the flag shipped — a refused bind was a WARN line and nothing else.

⚠️ THE WHOLE BUDGET IS 1000ms (`ABANDONMENT_BRIDGE_GRACE_MS`). Every millisecond here is time the compliance predicate counts as abandonment. Measured from the CARRIER's answer instant, so it includes webhook transit — deliberately, because the predicate counts that too.

READ BOTH SERIES TOGETHER. A bind that never happened records no latency, so a rollout watching only the p99 sees it IMPROVE as binds start failing. `result` is exactly one of three: `bound` is the success; `station_lost` means the station was not there — either gone before we reached for the socket, or the `reserved` frame was refused; `bind_failed` means the socket was live and the bridge declined it, and it is the one that means ROLL THE FLAG BACK rather than slow the pacing down.

Nothing else appears. An earlier version of this description named `no_agent` and `refused`, neither of which the code has ever emitted, and handed `station_lost` only half its meaning — worth knowing because the Grafana validator checks metric and label NAMES, not description prose, so a query written against that text would have returned nothing and looked like a healthy rollout.

ABORT if p99 crosses 150ms or any non-`bound` result is sustained.
panels.title: Agency Dialer — Late Bind (rollout abort criterion)

panels.description:
WHY abandoned calls reached no agent. Until this shipped, a bind failure and every other cause were the same increment in `agency_abandoned_total`, and they call for opposite responses.

`station_lost` — the agent's station was not there. A WORKSTATION problem: check sockets and wifi, do not touch the pacing. `bind_failed` — the socket was live and the bridge refused it: **roll the late-binding flag back.** `bridge_late` — it DID bridge, outside the 1s grace; a conversation happened and was merely late. `unattributed` — abandoned with no cause observed, which on the flag-off default path is the ordinary residual: the customer answered, an agent was bound at dial, and media never came up.

⚠️ `no_agent_available` is declared and **cannot currently occur**. Pacing is strictly 1:1 and the dialer refuses to dial once the station has gone, so nothing can dial with nobody free; it is the name reserved for a future pacing controller. If it ever appears without over-dialing having shipped, that is a bug, not a pacing signal. An earlier version of this panel told you it meant "slow the pacing down" — and the code was then labelling every flag-off station loss with it.

⚠️ A SEPARATE SERIES, not a `reason` label on `agency_abandoned_total`. Labelling that one would terminate it, and it is the compliance numerator read by the auto-pause guardrail's own cross-check. So `sum(rate(agency_abandoned_reason_total))` should TRACK `sum(rate(agency_abandoned_total))`; a persistent gap means an abandon path that reaches the compliance counter without declaring a reason.

`bridge_late` is the one that is not a failure to reach anybody — the call DID bridge, outside the 1s grace. It is still an abandoned call for compliance.

This panel is diagnosis. The compliance number is `agency_abandonment_rate_24h`, which is SQL-derived and taken with `max`.
panels.title: Agency Dialer — Abandonment Causes

panels.description:
How long wrap-up actually takes, by how it ended. The supervisor view already averages this in SQL, but there was no time series — so 'wrap-up is 18.5s mean against a 30s window' stayed a one-pilot artefact nobody could re-check.

`resolution` keeps it honest, for the same reason the attempt row records `wrapup_resolution`: a `forced` or `agent_left` wrap-up measures an interruption, not how long write-up work takes. Only `disposition_submitted`, `auto_return` and `agent_returned` are evidence.

THIS IS THE ONLY MEASUREMENT OF THE DISPOSITION-SPEED WORK. The pilot filed ZERO of 32 dispositions by keyboard; any drop in the `disposition_submitted` series after a hotkey or keyboard map ships is the entire result. Note most wrap-ups are TIMERLESS — held on an outstanding required disposition rather than a countdown — so this measures how fast agents file, not how long a window was configured.
panels.title: Agency Dialer — Wrap-up Duration

panels.description:
🚨 ALERT ON ANY SUSTAINED NON-ZERO. Each increment is a real person permanently removed from a campaign because WE failed to reach them — not because they were unavailable.

The our-fault redial ledger (`our_fault_attempts`, bound `OUR_FAULT_REDIAL_BOUND` = 3) exists so our own dropped sockets and cancelled dials do not spend a customer's retry allowance. But exhausting it writes the contact `exhausted`, and §11 records that this had NO SURFACE ANYWHERE: invisible in every view, with a plausible audit trail. This panel is that surface.

`outcome` makes it actionable, and there are THREE values with three different responses. `agent_disconnected` points at agent workstations — sockets, wifi, browser crashes. `canceled` points at our own teardown paths. `orphaned` points at replica crashes and leaked attempts: it is emitted by the REAPER, not the dial site, so it arrives on a different code path and in bursts after a restart rather than as a trickle. A rise in `orphaned` alone is an infrastructure signal and nothing to do with pacing or with agents. It is simultaneously a revenue loss and a list-quality lie, so it is worth paging on rather than reviewing weekly.

⚠️ The series has TWO PRODUCERS. `agency-dialer.ts` counts the dial-site retirements and `reaper.ts` counts the orphaned ones; an earlier version of this description explained only the dial site's two values, so the third would have appeared on the one panel that tells you to page with no gloss at all.

RELATED OPEN QUESTION: an `abandoned` attempt does NOT currently route to this ledger — it spends the customer's own allowance at `max_attempts: 2`, so two calls we dropped retire them. Whether that is right is a repeat-dial judgement recorded in §11, and `agency_abandoned_reason_total` is the evidence for deciding it.
panels.title: Agency Dialer — Contacts Retired by OUR Fault

panels.description: Supervisor notices sent when a campaign finishes, by result. `failed` (Mailjet refused or threw), `threw` and `claim_unavailable` (the delivery ledger was unwritable) page through `agy-campaign-mail-failures`.
panels.title: Campaign-Completion Emails

panels.description: What the insights rollup job still owes: dirty 15-minute buckets not yet recomputed (left axis) and the age of the oldest dirty mark (right axis), both as of the job's last pass (every 15s). Healthy is 0, or a few seconds while dialling; the Insights page says "updating" while the backlog is above 0. A backfill or a large rewrite shows as a spike that drains at about 200 buckets a batch. `agy-insights-rollup-behind` warns when the oldest mark stays over 120s for 10m. The gauges are set only when a pass finishes: a line frozen at one value while the batches line below is flat is a stalled pass (`agy-insights-rollup-stalled`). Empty before the job's first pass.
panels.title: Insights Rollup — Backlog and Oldest Dirty Mark

panels.description: Seconds one rollup batch takes (claim up to 200 marks, recompute their buckets from the attempts, commit). The empty batch that ends an idle pass is observed too, so an idle job sits near the bottom bucket. A pass batches for at most half an interval (7.5s), so a p95 near the 10s top bucket means each pass drains about one batch and a backlog grows: Postgres is slow, or the buckets are very large (8.1s was the slowest batch on a 1M-attempt campaign). Failed batches are not observed here; they are in the panel below.
panels.title: Insights Rollup — Batch Recompute Duration (p50 / p95)

panels.description: Per interval: rollup batches committed (the job's heartbeat: at least one per 15s pass while it runs), buckets recomputed, and failed batches (right axis, red). A failed batch rolls back with its marks kept and ends the pass, so a persistent failure is one per pass. `agy-insights-rollup-failing` warns at 10+ failures in 15m; `agy-insights-rollup-stalled` warns when the batches line has been flat for 15m.
panels.title: Insights Rollup — Batches, Buckets Recomputed and Failures

panels.description: Failed writes to the pacing history (`agency_campaign_pacing_minutes`), by path, and campaign-minutes dropped unwritten. `batch`: the pacing leader's 15s flush; a failed flush is kept and resent, so a short run of these loses nothing. `direct`: the single-row writes outside the tick (a wrap-up redial refused at the limit, an our-fault retirement); each one is a lost event. `dropped minutes`: the leader held more than 10,000 unwritten campaign-minutes and discarded the oldest; those minutes are gone from the Insights page's pacing history. Empty is healthy. `agy-pacing-history-write-failures` warns at 5+ failures in 15m, `agy-pacing-history-dropped` at any drop.
panels.title: Pacing History — Write Failures and Dropped Minutes

panels.description: How the pacing round splits each account's `max_concurrent_calls` between its running campaigns (MC1–MC7, docs/decisions.md). `in use` (solid): the campaign's own live attempts as the round saw them (`agency_campaign_slots_in_use`). `allocated` (dashed): those plus the slots the round granted it (`agency_campaign_slots_allocated`). Allocated above in use is a campaign being given new dials; equal is a campaign holding what it has. Free slots go to the campaign with the fewest live calls first, so campaigns of one account that share a busy limit converge on equal lines; one that cannot use its share (no agent ready, nothing due) leaves it to the others, and one above its share keeps its calls but gets nothing new until it is back at or under the others. Only campaigns of ONE account share slots: compare lines within an account. Both are set only after the campaign reports demand to a CONTENDED split (two or more of its account's campaigns contending) and cleared on every other tick outcome: no agent available, nothing due, a contended demand of 0, a tick that did not plan, any uncontended tick (a campaign alone on its account has no series), and when this process gives up its leadership. So a line that ends is a campaign leaving contention, not a campaign at 0. Set at each such report and exported once a minute, so each point is the last one before the export, not an average. `max` by campaign, so a series seen twice is not double-counted. The tenant filter does not apply: the series carry only `campaign_id`. A campaign held at 0 in use while the panel beside it shows it withheld is starved (`agy-pacing-share-starved`).
panels.title: Pacing Share — Slots In Use vs Allocated, per Campaign

panels.description: Slots the fair-share rule (MC1, docs/decisions.md) held back from a campaign while its account still had headroom: `min(demand, headroom) − grant`, counted for every campaign whose demand exceeded what it got, a tick that reported after its account's split closed (granted 0) included (`agency_pacing_share_withheld_total`, per second). This measures CONTENTION, not starvation: whenever an account's campaigns want more than its free lines, someone is withheld, and a busy campaign above an equal share is withheld routinely while its calls end. Empty means no contention; an account with one running campaign never withholds. STARVATION is a campaign withheld round after round while its `in use` line in the panel beside stays at 0: fewest-live-first should serve it before anyone, so either more of the account's campaigns tie at 0 live calls than it has lines (they take turns, so one always waits: raise the limit or run fewer campaigns at once), or its tick reports only after its account's split has closed (MC2: a tick that misses the 1 s wait but reports while the split is open still gets the leftover; after the close, at the latest the 5 s deadline, it gets 0) and so gets 0 every time, or the split itself is wrong. `agy-pacing-share-starved` warns after 10 minutes of it. The counter is sparse (a campaign's series starts at its first withheld slot), so `rate` misses that first one. The tenant filter does not apply: the series carry only `campaign_id`.
panels.title: Pacing Share — Slots Withheld per Campaign

panels.description: Report runs reaching a terminal state, by kind (agent, campaign, account) and status (ready, failed). A failed run ended without files; the run row's error.code says which stage failed. `agy-reports-failing` warns at 4+ failures in an hour. Empty until a run finishes.
panels.title: Reports — Runs Finished by Kind and Status

panels.description: Runs not yet finished, by status (queued, assembling, rendering), and the age of the oldest one (right axis), as of the reports tick's last pass (every 60s). Healthy is a few runs for a minute or two. Runs piling up in `queued` or `assembling` are the assembler; in `rendering`, the renderer or its callback (with the SQS renderer: the report-jobs queue, its dead-letter queue and the Lambda's logs in CloudWatch). `agy-reports-pending-too-long` warns when the oldest stays over 900s for 10m.
panels.title: Reports — Pending Runs and Oldest Pending

panels.description: Seconds to assemble a run's dataset (the screens' own reads, then the S3 upload), and from sending the render to applying its callback (queue wait, the renderer's cold start, Chromium and the workbook, the upload, the callback), by kind, p95. A render p95 approaching the Lambda's 300s timeout means renders are about to time out and be retried.
panels.title: Reports — Assembly and Render Duration (p95)

panels.description: Render callbacks by result (applied; stale: a fenced older attempt, harmless after a re-send; bad_signature: refused, `agy-reports-callback-bad-signature`; invalid: a body that did not parse), report-ready emails by result, and the runs subscriptions created (duplicate: a period that already had its run).
panels.title: Reports — Callbacks, Emails and Scheduled Runs

panels.description: Inbound calls ended per minute, by outcome: answered (an agent took it), overflow (nobody free before the route's maximum wait), overflow_no_capacity (over the route's max_concurrent, or no stream capacity), abandoned_in_queue (the caller hung up waiting), closed (out of hours, no route, a credential not active, or inbound switched off for the account), voicemail, rejected (a number not linked) and failed (answered, never got its media). `agy-inbound-calls-failed` warns on failed; `agy-inbound-unanswered-share` on the open-hours share that reached nobody.
panels.title: Inbound — Calls Ended by Outcome

panels.description: What the answer webhook answered the carrier, per minute: stream (our stream: the queue or a recorded message), spoken (a message the carrier speaks), hangup (refused before deciding: a number not linked), refused (a signature, token or nonce that did not verify), fallback (the answer failed) and timed_out (past its 4s budget); and the p95 answer time (right axis). Fallback and timed_out are callers told to try again (`agy-inbound-answer-fallback`); refused bursts are `agy-inbound-answer-refused`; a p95 above 2s is `agy-inbound-answer-slow`.
panels.title: Inbound — Answer Webhook by Result, and p95

panels.description: Callers waiting for an agent now, summed over routes (on offer excluded), and offers of a caller to an agent per minute by how each ended: connected, caller_left (hung up while offered), station_lost, lease_lost, refused (the call or the session was no longer free). Waiting with no offers for 15 minutes is `agy-inbound-callers-unserved`.
panels.title: Inbound — Callers Waiting and Offers by Result

panels.description: Seconds a caller waited in the queue (from first queueing), by how the wait ended: connected, abandoned, overflow or failed. A connected p95 near the route's maximum wait (120s by default) means callers only just reach someone; overflow sits at the maximum wait by definition.
panels.title: Inbound — Wait Time (p50 / p95) by How It Ended

panels.description: Of the calls that came in while their route was open (answered, overflow, overflow_no_capacity, abandoned_in_queue, voicemail), the share over the last hour that reached nobody (overflow, overflow_no_capacity, abandoned_in_queue). `agy-inbound-unanswered-share` warns above 0.5 with at least 10 such calls in the hour.
panels.title: Inbound — Open-Hours Calls That Reached Nobody (1h share)

panels.description: Whether this deployment puts inbound callers through to agents (1; 0 with MEDIA_WORKERS above 0, set at boot: `agy-inbound-connect-unavailable` while any credential has inbound enabled), and the credentials with inbound enabled by the last scheduled check of their Plivo Application (every 15 minutes): ok, url_mismatch or app_missing (its callers are refused: `agy-inbound-application-broken`), unreachable or failed (not checkable: `agy-inbound-application-unchecked`).
panels.title: Inbound — Connect Available and Application Health

panels.description: Rings of an away agent's phone for an inbound caller, per minute, by how each ended: answered, declined, busy_on_phone, expired, accept_lapsed, push_failed (agy-inbound-ring-push-failed), caller_left, answered_elsewhere (a station agent took the caller mid-ring) or cancelled. Expired and accept_lapsed are misses: two in a row stop the agent's phone ringing.
panels.title: Mode B — Rings by Result (per min)

panels.description: Seconds from the start of a ring to the agent tapping Answer on the phone (the ring window is 20 s). A p90 near 20 s means agents answer at the last moment; rings that are never answered are not in this histogram (see Rings by Result).
panels.title: Mode B — Ring to Answer (p50 / p90)

panels.description: Pushes to agents' phones (rings, ring_cancel, ring_off, test rings) per minute, by platform and result: ok, skipped, unregistered (the device is revoked), invalid, rate_limited, unavailable or unconfigured (the sender has no credentials).
panels.title: Mode B — Push Sends by Platform and Result (per min)
Active WebSocket Connections
panels.description: Open WebSockets by `type`. Only the WebRTC bridge's carrier leg is counted today (`type="webrtc_pstn"`); the agent's browser leg and the station socket are not instrumented. A bridged call with no matching socket is a stuck call.

panels.title: Telephony Lease Release Outcomes
panels.description: `failure` and `partial` both park concurrency leases — a slow leak of capacity that shows up later as calls rejected at the admission gate. Alert on the rate, not one occurrence.

panels.title: Provider Concurrency Admission
panels.description: Provider-mode telephony admissions by outcome. Rejected admissions are dials turned away at the telephony concurrency gate — capacity is full or a lease is parked (see Telephony Lease Release Outcomes).

Requests the rate limiter refused, by bucket and route class. `webhook`, `carrier_media` and `internal` clients cannot back off, so any sustained rate there is data loss (`agy-rate-limit-infra-rejected`, critical). `ip` holds every browser — consoles and agent stations, often many behind one office NAT (`agy-rate-limit-ip-rejected`, warning).
panels.title: Rate-Limit Rejections (429)
S3 Operations
panels.description: Recording, clip and contact-list storage: operations by result, and p95 duration.

Tenant carrier credentials (B19–B20), from the main process's housekeeping: a keyring check and a sweep at boot, then hourly. `missing key ids`: master key ids stored secrets are sealed under that TELEPHONY_CREDENTIAL_KEYS does not hold; every credential sealed under one cannot dial, hang up or check a webhook until the key is restored (0 is healthy; absent until the first check answers). `sweep ok` / `sweep failed`: sweep passes (shred revoked credentials whose calls have ended, drop secret versions past the rotation grace). `shredded`: credentials a sweep shredded. `agy-credential-keyring-missing-keys` pages on any missing key id, `agy-credential-sweep-failing` warns at 2+ failed sweeps in 3h.
panels.title: Carrier Credentials — Keyring and Sweeps

panels.description: Dials a carrier adapter gave up on after its own pre-send checks, by provider and kind (Plivo today). `auth_rejected`: the carrier refused the tenant's credential (401); every dial on it fails until a super-admin rotates or re-verifies it. `rate_limited`: the account's calls-per-second gate gave no slot in time, or the carrier answered 429; nothing was placed. `outcome_unknown`: a timeout, or a 2xx with no readable request id; the call may be placed, so the contact waits before its next dial. `refused`: any other non-2xx (403 is a destination outside the account's geo permissions). Empty is healthy.
panels.title: Carrier Dial Refusals

panels.description: Session authentication attempts by method and status. A rising `firebase` / `invalid_token` share means the server's `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` no longer matches the console's Firebase project (`agy-firebase-auth-rejected` pages above 50%). Super-admin sign-in has its own JWT and is not counted here.
panels.title: Sign-in Attempts

panels.description: Invite emails by role and result, and invite claims by result. `failed` emails mean invitees of that role never receive their only way in (`agy-invite-email-failures`); `identity_already_bound`, `cross_tenant_identity` and `address_required` (an admin-or-above invite presented by a sign-in that is not the invited address) claims in bursts read as account-takeover attempts (`agy-invite-claim-identity-conflicts`).
panels.title: Invites — Emails and Claims
Dialer Call Analysis
panels.description: Dialer-call analyses by terminal status, and the analysis queue by job status. A queue that grows while completions stay flat is a wedged worker.

panels.title: Dialer Analysis Latency (p95)
panels.description: `stage` is fetch | transcribe | analyze — which third of the dialer analysis pipeline is slow.

panels.title: Dialer Analysis Slots
panels.description: Analysis jobs running, and the share of DIALER_ANALYSIS_CONCURRENCY in use. Utilization pinned at 1 while the queued depth grows means the slots are the bottleneck: raise the concurrency (within the vendors' rate limits) or run another analysis process.

panels.title: Dialer Analysis Back-pressure
panels.description: Why free analysis slots are not claiming: waits for the recording memory budget (DIALER_ANALYSIS_MEMORY_BUDGET_BYTES), and pauses after an AI vendor rate limit. Reserved bytes are the recordings the slots hold.

Event-loop delay per export interval (the collector resets each collection). p99 for sustained lag, max for the single long block a p99 hides. Agency is one process, so a blocked loop delays every station message, pacing tick and bridged media frame. `agy-event-loop-delay-p99` warns above 0.5s for 10m.
panels.title: Event-Loop Delay (p99 / max)

panels.description: Share of each export interval the event loop was busy, 0..1. Also the liveness heartbeat: `agy-service-not-reporting` fires when this series stops for a deployment that reported in the last 7 days.
panels.title: Event-Loop Utilization

panels.description: V8 heap used across all spaces (`nodejs_heap_size_used_bytes`, one series per process). A climb that never comes back down is a leak; a heap near its limit shows up as event-loop delay (GC thrash).
panels.title: Heap Used

panels.description: Any series here means an agency metric has silently LOST ITS LABELS. When an instrument exceeds its cardinality limit (the OTel SDK default, 2000 attribute sets per instrument) the SDK folds every further attribute set into one `otel_metric_overflow="true"` series, so per-campaign / per-tenant panels for that metric under-report without going empty. The metric name is derived from the series name with any _bucket/_sum/_count suffix stripped. Expected empty; `agy-metric-cardinality-overflow` alerts on it.
panels.title: Telemetry — Cardinality-Overflow Series
Feature Flag Evaluations
panels.description: Which feature flags agency evaluates and how they resolve.

panels.title: ERROR / FATAL Log Volume (Loki)
panels.description: ERROR and FATAL lines per interval, from Loki. Requires the `loki_datasource` variable (Grafana Cloud: `grafanacloud-logs`). severity_number >= 17 is OTel ERROR and above. The `agy-error-log-volume` rule pages on 10+ in 15m. Logs reach Loki only through the OTel SDK, so this is empty exactly when metrics are (OTEL_ENABLED, endpoint and OTEL_SERVICE_NAME must all be set).

Each process's loop, by `instance` (`<host>:primary`, `:media0`, `:analysis0`, …, docs/scaling.md §7). With media workers the primary should sit low while the workers carry the audio; a worker pinned near 1 is saturated. One series per process; in one-process mode, one series.
panels.title: Event-Loop Utilization by Process

panels.description: Child exits seen by the primary. `expected=false` is a crash: the slot is reaped and re-forked; more than WORKER_CRASH_LOOP_MAX in 5 minutes makes the primary exit. `agy-cluster-child-crash` pages on any media crash.
panels.title: Child Process Exits

panels.description: Requests between the primary and its children (dial.execute, core.inject, carrier.webhook, reaper.snapshot, …). A rising `timeout` share for one type means the receiving process's loop is behind.
panels.title: IPC Requests by Type and Outcome

panels.description: Upgrades the primary handed to a media worker (`handed_off`) or refused with 503 (`no_owner`: the owning worker is down or the carrier URL has no slot; `buffered` / `not_sent` / `unsupported` should stay at zero).
panels.title: WebSocket Handoffs

list.label: Prometheus
list.name: datasource
list.description: Prometheus / Mimir datasource. On Grafana Cloud this is `grafanacloud-prom`.

list.label: Loki
list.name: loki_datasource
list.description: Loki datasource, used only by the error-log panel. On Grafana Cloud this is `grafanacloud-logs`.

list.label: Environment
list.name: environment
list.description: PRIMARY FILTER. The `deployment_environment` resource attribute (OTEL_ENVIRONMENT, falling back to NODE_ENV), listed from agency's own deployments only (its runtime gauge, one series per process).

list.label: Service
list.name: service_name
list.description: Agency's deployments: magick-agency (production), magick-agency-Staging, magick-agency-Dedicated, from OTEL_SERVICE_NAME. All means `magick-agency(-.+)?` — the same regex the alert rules select (agency_service_name_regex in grafana/terraform/variables.tf; the validators keep them equal), so no other service ever appears here.

list.label: Tenant
list.name: tenant_id
list.description: Scopes the per-tenant agency panels (those whose metric carries tenant_id). Listed from settled attempts, so a tenant appears once it has dialled.
